duplicate_gate.selected_construct: Retinitis pigmentosa — preferential early rod photoreceptor degeneration

option_audit.rods: Uniquely best: typical RP is rod-predominant early; this directly explains nyctalopia followed by peripheral-field constriction.
option_audit.cones: Cone-rod dystrophy can preferentially affect cones, but typical RP has early rod-predominant dysfunction; cone-first disease instead emphasizes central acuity, color vision, and photophobia before peripheral/dark-adaptation loss.
option_audit.retinal_pigment_epithelium: RPE abnormalities and pigment migration contribute to the bone-spicule appearance, but in typical RP the early disease phenotype is driven by rod photoreceptor dysfunction/degeneration.
option_audit.retinal_ganglion_cells: RGCs are retinal output neurons and are not the preferential early degenerating photoreceptor population in typical RP.
option_audit.bipolar_cells: Bipolar cells relay rod/cone input to inner retinal neurons and are not the preferential early primary cell population lost in typical RP.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Progressive night blindness plus peripheral-field constriction, preserved reading vision, bilateral bone-spicule pigmentation, and attenuated retinal vessels independently reconstruct classic retinitis pigmentosa. The mechanism question then maps the early phenotype to rod photoreceptors.
adversarial_second_pass.genetic_heterogeneity_attack: RP is genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous. The item deliberately asks about the typical form; authoritative GeneReviews and StatPearls sources specifically support early rod-predominant dysfunction in typical RP, so the answer is not universalized to every inherited retinal dystrophy.
adversarial_second_pass.cone_rod_dystrophy_attack: Cone-rod dystrophy may have similar fundus findings but typically causes central acuity loss, photophobia, and color-vision defects before peripheral visual loss and defective dark adaptation, the opposite sequence from this vignette.
adversarial_second_pass.vitamin_A_deficiency_attack: Vitamin A deficiency can cause nyctalopia, but it does not best explain this chronic progressive bilateral rod-cone dystrophy phenotype with classic RP fundus findings.
adversarial_second_pass.congenital_stationary_night_blindness_at: Congenital stationary night blindness is nonprogressive and therefore does not fit years of progressive peripheral-field loss with classic RP fundus changes.
adversarial_second_pass.RPE_attack: Bone-spicule pigment arises from RPE migration, but that does not make RPE the preferential early cell population responsible for the typical rod-first functional syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.second_answer_search: No alternative option explains both the temporal sequence and the cell-level mechanism as well as rod photoreceptors.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: The fundus findings establish the disease construct but do not directly state the tested cell population; answering still requires foundational retinal physiology/pathophysiology.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No dose, numeric threshold, inheritance percentage, ERG cutoff, treatment rule, or universal age-of-onset claim is required.
